claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the current record because aggregate readiness passes and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, with the emergency-shelter regression handled through explicit release documentation rather than prior approval or informal monitoring.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Material weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed before launch unless covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring comments may provide context but cannot substitute for current evidence meeting the policy predicate.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support readiness but do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure requirement for the regressed slice.
evidence_requests: Provide the current model card or release documentation showing the emergency-shelter-placement weakness is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
If disclosure is not present, provide an approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record covering this regression before launch.
Provide the materiality assessment or review record establishing whether the 1.5-point regression is treated as a material limitation under policy.
specific_concerns: Policy makes current disclosure or approved mitigation a prerequisite to certification for a material named-use-case weakness.
The admissible record shows a current emergency-shelter-placement regression below the warning threshold.
The admissible record does not show that current release documentation already discloses that regression.
The release-thread monitoring comment is not documented as reviewed mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or disclosure language.
Prior approval of the model family is stale context and cannot satisfy the current-release predicate after the configuration change and new eval batch.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify now is not fully supported because no admissible evidence shows the required disclosure is already present in the current release documentation.
The statement that certification is supportable on the current record overreaches unless the current documentation artifact containing the limitation disclosure is produced.
